description: Every retrieval technique implemented in this work, what it measured, and whether it ships. Recorded so each decision is reproducible and so a decision can EXPIRE — hybrid search was rejected, then adopted when the corpus grew.

techniques.name: Relevance floor
techniques.note: Bands overlap (on-topic worst 1.548, off-topic best 1.426) so it cannot be tightened.

techniques.name: Hybrid BM25 + RRF
techniques.evidence: 362 chunks: lost at every beta. 1354 chunks: recall +0.091, MAP +0.091
techniques.note: REVERSED. The technique did not change; the corpus did. Only 10% keyword weight is correct.

techniques.name: Per-source cap
techniques.note: Largest single gain. FAO 589 was taking all 3 slots on 10 of 33 queries.

techniques.name: PDF cleaning
techniques.evidence: 13 structural pages dropped; running header in 4/992 chunks instead of 111/1034
techniques.note: A table of contents is not knowledge under any corpus conditions.

techniques.name: Header chunking (markdown)
techniques.note: 95% of sections are smaller than the chunk window, so splitting fragments rather than aligns.

techniques.name: PDF chapter labelling
techniques.note: Extraction works (29%->95% coverage by forward-fill); it is the PREFIXING that loses.

techniques.name: Cross-encoder reranking
techniques.note: ms-marco model is out of domain for operator phrasing against agronomy prose.

techniques.name: Query rewriting
techniques.note: Three prefix/expansion techniques already lost for the same reason; adding vocabulary to a corpus that shares one vocabulary domain dilutes rather than disambiguates.

the_pattern: Four of the eight measured techniques LOST, and three of those four share one mechanism: they add topic words (a section crumb, a chapter name, a heading) to chunks in a corpus where every document already shares a vocabulary domain. Words that appear in every chunk about a topic carry no discriminating information — they only dilute the distinctive content already in the vector. What DID work was structural instead of lexical: refusing irrelevant passages, refusing error pages, and refusing to let one source occupy every slot.
